DOCK_PROMPT:
You are reviewing a family-history conversation transcript. A diagram was
extracted from it, but some extracted family members ended up disconnected from
the main family tree. Your single job: find the stated family connection (if
any) between each floating group and the main tree.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
- The connecting evidence is often a third-person pronoun or kinship reference
  (e.g. "that was her sister..."). You MUST resolve such references to their
  antecedent across conversation turns: work out who "her"/"his"/"their"
  refers to from the surrounding dialogue, then emit the edge to THAT person.
- One transcript speaker is the diagram owner describing THEIR OWN family.
  That speaker IS in the main tree: the proband node (named "User" when
  present, otherwise the person whose partners and children match what the
  speaker describes). First-person evidence ("I", "my", "me") from that
  speaker anchors to the proband's id — e.g. "I dated her in college" emits
  the floating ex-partner partner_of the proband.
- Emit edges ONLY for floating-group members, anchored ONLY to main-tree ids.
- relation meanings: member is partner_of anchor; member is child_of anchor;
  member is parent_of anchor; member is sibling_of anchor.
- partner_of covers ALL romantic pair-bonds, past or present: spouses,
  ex-spouses, ex-girlfriends/boyfriends, dating relationships. A past romance
  that ended without marriage still attaches: partner_of with married=false.
  On partner_of edges set married=true if the couple is or was married,
  married=false if the relationship is or was romantic but never a marriage
  (dating, girlfriend/boyfriend, ex-partner); leave married unset when not
  stated.
- Every edge MUST include a VERBATIM quote: ONE contiguous span copied exactly
  from the transcript. NEVER stitch separate sentences together with "..." and
  never paraphrase — a stitched or edited quote is rejected and the edge is
  lost. The quote must evidence the RELATION TYPE you assert — romantic
  involvement for partner_of, a parent/child statement for child_of/parent_of.
  If the person's name and the relation evidence sit in different turns, quote
  the contiguous span carrying the relation evidence and explain the name
  resolution in `reasoning`. For child_of/parent_of edges restate in
  `reasoning` which side is the parent generation.
- If the transcript never states how a group connects, verdict "none" with no
  edges. Do NOT guess or invent. A friend, colleague, or acquaintance with no
  stated romantic involvement is not family: verdict "none".

MAIN TREE (id, name):
{roster}

{floats}

TRANSCRIPT:
{transcript}

Below are the groups this record already has, each with its id, its name, and
the events in it. Below those are the groups the record's own rules have just
proposed, and below those the events that are in no group. Return the record's
groups as they should now stand.

its events. Someone has read that name before. Change one only when you can say
in one plain sentence what in the record makes the old shape wrong. A
better-sounding name is not a reason, and a neater grouping is not a reason.

**Put each new event where it belongs.** An event in no group joins the group
whose story it is part of: close to it in time, about the same people, or the
later consequence of what opened that group. If it belongs nowhere, leave it
out. Events months or years later can still belong to a group.

asked again.

Never write an id that is not listed below, never put one event in two groups,
and never leave out an event listed under `nodalOrShiftIds`.

Every group you return holds at least three events. One or two events on their

tool_meanings.kind: Which kind of event this is. Use noted for anything worth writing down that is not a birth, adoption, marriage, bonding, separation, divorce, death or shift — a move, a new job, finishing a course. A noted event must say what happened in its description.
tool_meanings.description: What happened, with no names of the people this event links: the person, spouse, child and targets are said by their fields.
tool_meanings.location: Where it happened, when the conversation says where. On a noted event about a move it is the place they moved to.
tool_meanings.person: The person the event is about. On a marriage, bonding, separation or divorce it is one of the two partners and spouse is the other. On a birth or adoption it is a parent, and is left out when the parents are not known — never the same id as child.
tool_meanings.spouse: The other partner. Required with person on married, bonded, separated and divorced; on a birth it is the second parent.
tool_meanings.child: For a birth or adoption, who was born or taken in: set child, not person.
tool_meanings.anxiety: Which way this variable moved, if it moved.
tool_meanings.symptom: Which way this variable moved, if it moved.
tool_meanings.functioning: Which way this variable moved, if it moved.
tool_meanings.relationship: Which relationship value this event carries.
tool_meanings.relationship_targets: The other people this event's relationship links. Required whenever relationship is set, and never empty.
tool_meanings.relationship_triangles: A second list of people the relationship links. Required when relationship is inside or outside.
tool_meanings.person_a: One side of the bond. A bond is between two different people and there is one bond ever between any two of them.
tool_meanings.person_b: The other side. Leave it out only when nobody named them: the record then adds them as a generically named person, because a bond with one side is not a bond.
tool_meanings.parents: The id of the pair bond this person was born into. Children are the offspring of a bond, so the two parents must have one first.
